children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child does not live with claimant and weekly upkeep (£10.00) is below the Child Benefit rate (£26.05)
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand more about your situation.

**First question: Do you have a child (or children) you're claiming for?**

If yes, please tell me:
- How old is your child (or children)?
- If you have multiple children, please share their ages

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to your situation. The rules differ based on whether a child is:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old (requires education/training check)
- 20 or over (generally not eligible)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you! Since Alex is 8 years old, he falls under the "under 16" category. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - for a child under 16 like Alex, we need to check a few more requirements.

**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

At 8 years old, Alex is likely not working at all, which would mean the answer is "yes" - but I want to confirm this with you to make sure we're assessing everything correctly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 8, so no, he's not in any paid work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

This means - is Alex receiving benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name?

For most 8-year-olds, they wouldn't be receiving these types of benefits in their own right, so the answer would typically be "yes, that's correct - he's NOT receiving these benefits." Can you confirm this is the case for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue to the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

This is specifically about whether he's enrolled in an apprenticeship program. At 8 years old, this almost certainly doesn't apply, but I need to confirm:

Is Alex NOT in any apprenticeship? (The answer should be "yes, that's correct - he's not in an apprenticeship")

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. He's only 8, so that doesn't apply to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check **your residency status** as the claimant.

**Question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if **ANY** of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common route)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these situations applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You can qualify if **ANY** of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common situation)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like his clothes and other bits and pieces - I give about £10 a week.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me check the current Child Benefit rates to see if your contribution meets the requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that the specific Child Benefit payment rates aren't included in my reference data. Let me clarify your situation:

You're contributing about £10 per week towards Alex's care. To qualify under the "contributing to upkeep" route, you need to pay **at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment** (or provide equivalent support in kind like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents).

The current Child Benefit rate for the eldest or only child is approximately **£25.60 per week** (though you should verify the exact current rate).

**A few questions to help determine if you meet the responsibility requirement:**

1. Is your £10 per week contribution in addition to other support you provide (like buying clothes, presents, paying for activities, etc.)?
2. When you add up all your financial contributions and support in kind over a week or month, does it equal or exceed approximately £25-26 per week?
3. Do you have a maintenance agreement or court order in place?

Or alternatively - do you ever have Alex stay with you, even if it's not his main residence?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the £10 a week is what I contribute - that's it. I don't have a court order or anything formal like that. And no, Alex doesn't stay with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Based on what you've told me, let me assess your situation:

You're contributing £10 per week, but the Child Benefit rate for one child is approximately £25-26 per week. To qualify under the "contributing to upkeep" path, you need to contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount.

Since:
- Alex doesn't live with you
- Your contribution (£10/week) is below the Child Benefit threshold (~£25-26/week)
- You don't have a formal maintenance agreement

Unfortunately, this means you don't meet the responsibility requirement for claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment - Result

**I'm sorry, but you are NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why you're not eligible:

While Alex meets all the child-related requirements (he's 8 years old, not working, not receiving benefits, not in an apprenticeship), and you meet the UK residency requirement, **you do not meet the responsibility requirement**.

To be considered "responsible" for a child under Child Benefit rules, you must either:
- Live with the child, OR
- Contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit payment (approximately £25-26 per week) towards their care

Your contribution of £10 per week falls below this threshold, and Alex doesn't live with you.

### What this means:

The person who **does** live with Alex (likely his other parent or guardian) would be the one eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, as they have primary responsibility for his care.

### Your options:

- If you want to be eligible in the future, you could increase your financial contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate (currently around £25-26 per week)
- You could formalize a maintenance agreement that meets the threshold
- The person Alex lives with should claim Child Benefit if they haven't already

If you have any questions about this decision or your situation has changed, please let me know. You can also find more information at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old, which meets the age requirement (under 16). Alex is not in paid work, doesn't receive benefits in his own right, and isn't in an apprenticeship - all of which satisfy the child-related criteria. The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester), meeting the residency requirement. However, the claimant does not meet the responsibility requirement. Alex does not live with the claimant, and the claimant's financial contribution of £10 per week falls below the Child Benefit payment threshold of approximately £25-26 per week. There is no formal maintenance agreement or court order in place. Therefore, the claimant is not considered responsible for Alex under Child Benefit rules.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because they do not meet the responsibility requirement - Alex doesn't live with them and their financial contribution (£10/week) is below the required threshold (approximately £25-26/week equivalent to Child Benefit payment).
